title: Add pagination to the blog post index
description: The blog index (GET /) currently returns ALL posts with no pagination (blog.py:16 — SELECT ... ORDER BY created DESC returns unbounded results). This is a performance risk if the post count grows. Pagination should limit results per page and provide navigation.
notes: Resolved: index() now reads a 1-based `page` query param (invalid/<1 falls back to page 1), counts total posts, and queries with LIMIT ?/OFFSET ? at POSTS_PER_PAGE=10. index.html renders Newer/Older nav links gated on has_prev/has_next. Tests test_index_pagination (page-sized subset + next/prev links across two pages) and test_index_ignores_invalid_page cover the behavior; 35 passed, blog.py 100% coverage, ruff clean.
spec:
1. Add a per-page limit (e.g. 10 or 20 posts) to the index query using LIMIT and OFFSET.
2. Add a page query parameter (e.g. /?page=2) to control which page of posts is returned.
3. Add next/previous navigation links to flaskr/templates/blog/index.html.
4. Add a test verifying that the index returns only the page-sized subset of posts.
5. Verify the index still works without a page parameter (defaults to page 1).
